item.title: The Discrete Mathematics Hiding Inside LLMs
item.description:
A recent LinkedIn conversation got me thinking about unexpected connections. Someone posted about taking discrete mathematics and finding it abstract, disconnected from real software engineering. I replied that predicate logic maps almost directly onto how LLMs structure inference. What felt theoretical becomes very applied very fast.

That exchange stuck with me. The more I thought about it, the more I realized how much discrete mathematics lives inside systems that seem purely statistical. LLMs are often described in terms of neural networks, gradient descent, and probability distributions. That’s all true. But underneath the calculus and linear algebra, the same structures you learn in a discrete math course keep appearing: sets, predicates, Boolean operations, modular arithmetic, formal proof patterns.

This post traces those connections. If you’ve taken discrete mathematics and wondered what it has to do with modern AI, the answer is: more than you’d expect.

“Every attention head is a predicate. Every mask is a set operation. Every chain-of-thought is a proof.”
